full_judgment: 2. Relevant facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are that the present respondents No.2- 5 as plaintiffs filed Arpito Sampatti Suit No. 140 of 2012, before the Court of Arpito Sampatti Prottarpan Tribunal, Narsingdi stating, inter alia, that one Jagobondo Shaha was the owner of 110 decimals of the land appertaining to CS Khatian No. 272 and CS Plots No. 91, 185, 324 and 325. Said Jagobondo Shaha died leaving behind four sons namely Debendra Nath Shaha, Grenenda Nath Shaha, Nepal Chandra Shaha, and Gopal Chandra Shaha. Accordingly, S.A. Khatian No. 355 and SA Plots No. 91, 185, 324, and 325 in respect of said land was prepared in the name of said four sons of Jagobondo Shaha. Subsequently, Grenenda Nath Shaha, Nepal Chandra Shaha, and Gopal Chandra Shaha left for India. Debendra Nath Shaha died in Bangladesh leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs. The plaintiffs are still living in Bangladesh. Despite the said facts, the said land was enlisted in the "Ka" schedule as vested property in the Bangladesh Gazette, Additional Issue dated 16-4-2012, page No. 15089 under serial No. 179 of Mouza Nondipara District-Narsingdi, vide VP Case No. 22 of 1976 dated 3-7-1977. The plaintiffs are in possession of 82 decimals of the said land taking the same lease from the Government. After the enactment of the Arpito Sampatti Prottarpan Ain, 2001, being a co-owner, respondents No. 2-5 as the plaintiffs instituted the suit for releasing the property from the "Ka" schedule. The present petitioner as defendant contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying the materials averments made in the plaint. During the trial both the parties adduced both oral and documentary evidence in support of their claim.
